rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A poor guardian may take from an orphan's assets in proportion to the work and benefit he provides, without extravagance or waste.
rows.anchor: يأكل الفقير إذا ولى مال اليتيم بقدر قيامه على ماله ومنفعته له مالم يسرف أو يبذر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In answer to Ibn Umar, the Prophet permitted eating from an orphan's wealth without extravagance, accumulating wealth, or using it to shield one's own assets.
rows.anchor: سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : ليس لي مال وإني ولي يتيم فقال : كل من مال يتيمك غير مسرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether the guardian's permitted consumption counts as wages has two opinions; the author's school takes the second, as al-Jassas states in al-Ahkam.
rows.anchor: وهل يعد ذلك أجرة أم لا قولان ومذهبنا الثاني كما صرح به الجصاص في الأحكام

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وأبي العالية والزهري وعبيدة السلماني والباقر
rows.claim: A poor guardian may borrow enough from the orphan's property for his needs and repay it once able; this is the recognized manner of eating.
rows.anchor: أن للولي الفقير أن يأكل من مال اليتيم بقدر الكفاية على جهة القرض فإذا وجد ميسرة أعطى ما أستقرض

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar treated the public treasury like an orphan's property: he abstained when wealthy, took a reasonable amount when needy, and repaid it when able.
rows.anchor: إن أستغنيت أستعففت وإن أحتجت أخذت منه بالمعروف فإذا أيسرت قضيت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ata, says the permission was abrogated by the warning against consuming orphan property wrongfully.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال : ( ومن كان فقيرا ) الآية نسختها ( إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما )

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One reported view permits a poor guardian to take food from the orphan's wealth but not clothing.
rows.anchor: ذهب قوم إلى إباحة الأكل دون الكسوة ورواه عكرمة عنإبن عباس

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد
rows.claim: The view that the verse authorizes spending the orphan's own wealth on the orphan according to his circumstances is rejected: it does not explain the command to abstain, and disrupts the syntax.
rows.anchor: وحكى ذلك عن يحيى بن سعيد وهو مردودلأن قوله سبحانه : ( فليستعفف ) لا يعطي معنى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The handover clause addresses guardians and trustees: after observing the preceding requirements, they deliver the assets under their care to the orphans; fronting the recipient emphasizes them.
rows.anchor: أيها الأولياء والأوصياء إليهم أي اليتامى بع رعاية ماذكر لكم أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing the handover establishes receipt and discharges the guardian, reducing suspicion and disputes and better preserving trust; the author's school treats it as recommended.
rows.anchor: بأن قبضوها وبرئت عنها ذممكم لما أن ذلك أبعد عن التهمة وأنفى للخصومة وأدخل في الأمانة وهو أمر ندب عندنا

rows.speaker: الشافعية والمالكية
rows.claim: The Shafi'i and Maliki schools regard witnessing the transfer as obligatory and infer that a guardian cannot prove delivery merely by his assertion.
rows.anchor: وذهب الشافعية والمالكية إلى أنه أمر وجوب وأستدلوا بذلك على أن القيم لا يصدق بقوله في الدفع بدون بينة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets God's sufficiency as witness for the parties.
rows.anchor: وكفى بالله حسيبا 6 ( أي شهيدا قاله السدي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says that no witness is better than God between guardians and orphans, matching the author's view that formal proof is not required.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أن معنى ( وكفى بالله حسيبا ) أنه لا شاهد أفضل من الله تعالى فيما بينكم وبينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God suffices as your reckoner, so do not disobey the command or exceed its limits; this is apt because trustees are accountable for what they hold.
rows.anchor: فلا تخالفوا ما أمرتم به ولا تجاوزوا ما حد لكم ولا يخفى موقع المحاسب هنا لأن الوصي يحاسب على ما في يده

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa analyzes 'God suffices' either with God as subject and an extra ba conveying command, or with an implicit subject and God as object; hasiban is circumstantial or specification.
rows.anchor: وفي فاعل ( كفى ) كما قال أبو البقاء : وجهان أحدهما أنه الاسم الجليل والباء زائدة

rows.speaker: السمين
rows.claim: Al-Samin treats kafa as taking one object, while Abu al-Baqa allows two, with the implied sense of God sparing you harm or the like.
rows.anchor: وكفى ) متعدية إلى مفعول واحد عند السمين والتقدير وكفاكم الله حسيبا وإلى مفعولين عند أبي البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Esoterically, piety means fearing disobedience and attachment to worldly others, while keeping the primordial covenant made when people testified about themselves.
rows.anchor: أي أحذوره من المخالفات والنظر إلى الأغيار وألزموا عهد الأزل حين أشهدكم على أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'single soul' is the Muhammadan Reality, also called the universal rational soul, the world's heart, and the real Adam, father of the historical Adam.
rows.anchor: وهي الحقيقة المحمدية ويعبر عنها أيضا بالنفس الناطقة الكلية التي هي قلب العالم وبآدم الحقيقي الذي هو الأب لآدم

rows.speaker: ابن الفارض
rows.claim: Ibn al-Farid's cited verse has the Reality say that although outwardly a son of Adam, it bears within itself the meaning of fatherhood.
rows.anchor: وإني وإن كنت إبن آدم صورة فلي فيه معنى شاهد بأبوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spouse is either nature or the animal soul arising from the first soul; it was created on the side facing the created realm, symbolized by the left rib, as that side is farther from the Real.
rows.anchor: وهي الطبيعة أو النفس الحيوانية الناشئة منها وقد خلقت من الجهة التي تلي عالم الكون وهو الضلع الأيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Esoterically, the many men are perfected people inclining toward their father, while women are deficient people inclining toward their mother.
rows.anchor: أي كاملين يميلون إلى أبيهم ( ونساءا ) ناقصين يميلون إلى أمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling upon God means denying independent existence, since God manifested people's determinations after they were nothing; piety toward wombs means loving God's saints, the true kinship of the higher principles.
rows.anchor: فلا تثبتوا لأنفسكم وجودا مع وجوده لأنه الذي أظهر تعيناتكم بعد أن لم تكونوا شيئا مذكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God watches hearts; inclination to anything besides Him and suspicion of the people of His presence drive away the lights, leaving the heart desolate.
rows.anchor: إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا ) ناظرا إلى قلوبكم مطلعا على ما فيها فإذا رأى فيها الميل إلى السوي وسوء الظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orphans are spiritual faculties deprived of nurture from their father, the Holy Spirit; their property is their share of spiritual perfections.
rows.anchor: وهم يتامى القوى الروحانية المنقطعين عن تربية الروح القدسي الذي هو أبوهم ( أموالهم ) وهي حقوقهم من الكمالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Swapping bad for good means relinquishing good traits for bad ones; consuming their property with one's own means mixing truth with falsehood, a great veil.
rows.anchor: بأن تعطوا الطيب من الصفات وتذيلوه وتأخذوا بدله الخبيث منها وتتصفوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of failing to nurture the spiritual faculties justly points to marriage reducing desire and protecting chastity, which aids their discipline and purification from indecency.
rows.anchor: لتقل شهواتكم وتحفظوا فروجكم فتستعينوا بذلك على التربية لما يحصل لكم من التزكية عن الفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one cannot treat multiple wives justly, one wife suffices to achieve the spiritual purpose.
rows.anchor: فواحدة ) تكفيكم في تحصيل غرضكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dowries are God's gift and favor; giving them also symbolizes purification from miserliness and treachery and adornment with fidelity and generosity, which disciplines the faculties.
rows.anchor: عطية من الله وفضلا وفيه إشارة إلى التخلية عن البخل والغدر والتحلية بالوفاء والكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wife's willing gift of part of her dowry may be received pleasantly; this trains the recipient away from pride and toward humility and compassion.
rows.anchor: ولا تأنفوا وتتكبروا عن ذلك وهذا أيضا نوع من التربية لما فيه من التخلية عن الكبر والأنفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foolish are people below perfection: do not entrust them with spiritual secrets and knowledge; feed them some of it, adorn them with it, and speak aptly so they submit and follow.
rows.anchor: لا تودعوا الناقصين عن مراتب الكمال أسراركم وعلومكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Testing the orphans signifies testing deficient wayfarers; reaching marriage means becoming ready for guidance, and sound judgment means steadiness on the path without fickleness.
rows.anchor: ولعله إشارة إلى إختبار الناقصين من السائرين ( حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح ) وصلحوا للأرشاد والتربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Handing over the wealth means entrusting spiritual secrets only to free and worthy people.
rows.anchor: فأدفعوا إليهم أموالهم ) التي يستحقونها من الأسرار التي لا تودع إلا عند الأحرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perfect shaykhs are charged to appoint successors and authorize disciples who are fit to guide others.
rows.anchor: والمراد إيصاء الكمل من الشيوخ أن يخلفوا ويأذنوا بالإرشاد من يصلح لذلك من المريدين السالكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not consuming the disciples' wealth means not benefiting from their spiritual gifts to their exclusion or rushing before they mature into guidance; this is a grave disease of the ego.
rows.anchor: أي تنتفعوا بتلك الأموال دونهم ( إسرافا وبدارا أن يكبروا ) بالتصدي للأرشاد فإن ذلك من أعظم أدواء النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spiritually rich guardian should abstain from a disciple's resources; one unable to bear need may benefit only to necessity's measure.
rows.anchor: ومن كان منكم غنيا ) بالله لا يلتفت إلى ضرورات الحياة أصلا ( فليستعفف ) عما للمريد ( ومن كان فقيرا ) لا يتحمل الضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spiritual handover calls for witnessing God and the spirits of the divine presence and taking a covenant that the disciple honor rights owed to God and creation.
rows.anchor: فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم ) الله تعالى وأرواح أهل الحضرة وخذوا العهد عليهم برعاية الحقوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is true existence and sees hidden betrayals and inward secrets; He is the sufficient protector.
rows.anchor: لأنه الموجود الحقيقي والمطلع الذي يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور وهو حسبنا ونعم الوكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers are the previously described disbelievers; the relative clause replaces a pronoun to show their loss results from denying and persisting in denial of meeting God.
rows.anchor: هم الكفار الذين حكيت أحوالهم لكن وضع الموصول موضع الضمير للايذان بتسبب خسرانهم عما في حيز الصلة من التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi reports that meeting God means meeting what He promised, citing Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan; other exegetes supply reward or take the phrase as a representation of resurrection and its sequel.
rows.anchor: والمراد به لقاء ما وعد سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes make the implicit complement 'meeting God's reward'; others read meeting God as a representative metaphor for resurrection and what follows.
rows.anchor: وصرح بعضهم بتقدير المضاف أي لقاء جزاء بالله تعالى وصرح آخرون بأن لقاء الله تعالى استعارة تمثيلية عن البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is the appointed Judgment Day; saʿah originally means a short stretch of time and became the name of the known time, either because it is brief beside eternity or its reckoning is swift.
rows.anchor: وأصل الساعة القطعة من الزمان وغلبت على الوقت المعلوم كالنجم للثريا وسمي ساعة لقلته بالنسبة لما بعده من الخلود

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Some interpret the Hour here as the time of death.
rows.anchor: وفسرها بعضهم هنا بوقت الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'until' may mark the end of their denial, or the end of loss in its ordinary sense: like Satan's curse lasting until Judgment, they then meet a calamity that eclipses earlier losses.
rows.anchor: غاية الخسران لكن بالمعنى المتعارف والكلام حينئذ على حد قوله تعالى : وان عليك لعنتيلعنتي إلى يوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghtah means suddenly, without awareness; it can be a circumstantial verbal noun of the subject or object, or a cognate accusative of the verb or an implied verb.
rows.anchor: أي فجأو وبغتة بالتحريك مثلها وبغتة كمنعة فجأة أي هجم عليه من غير شعور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer the conditional with 'O our remorse'; this personifies remorse and summons it as though it could arrive at its appointed moment.
rows.anchor: نداء للحسرة وهي شدة الندم كأنه قيل : يا حسرتنا تعالى فهذا أوانك

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies 'be present, O remorse'; this figurative summons alerts them to the causes of regret, since remorse itself cannot literally be called or arrive.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : التقدير يا حسرة احضري هذا أو انك وهو نداء مجازي ومعناه تنبيه أنفسهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The cited prophetic saying that whoever dies has had his resurrection occur explains why death may be treated as the beginning of the Hour.
rows.anchor: من مات فقد قامت قيامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafrit means neglecting what one was able to do; Abu Ubayda glosses it as waste, while Ibn Bahr derives it from going ahead and leaving precedence to another.
rows.anchor: فالتفريط التقصير فيما قدر على فعله وقال أبو عبيدة معناه التضييع وقال ابن بحر : معناه السبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn Bahr's derivation, the doubled consonant conveys removal, as in scraping and stripping the camel's hide.
rows.anchor: فالتضعيف فيه للسلب كجلدت البعير أرلت جلده وسلبته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'therein' may refer to worldly life, according to Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: أي الحياة الدنيا كما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes 'therein' to refer to the Hour, meaning failure to prepare for it through faith and good deeds.
rows.anchor: أو في الساعة كما روي عن الحسن والمراد من التفريط في الساعة التقصير في مراعاة حقها والاستعداد لها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the pronoun refers to Paradise, meaning that they failed to seek it; al-Alusi considers this reading remote.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير للجنة أي على ما فرطنا في طلبها ونسب إلى السدي ولا يخفى بعده

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi cites a report from the Prophet, through al-Aʿmash, Abu Salih and Abu Saʿid, that the Fire's inhabitants see their places in Paradise and lament; al-Alusi says this cannot settle the interpretation while other possibilities remain.
rows.anchor: ما رواه الأعمش عن أبي صالح عن أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في هذه الآية : يرى أهل النار منازلهم من الجنة

rows.speaker: محمد بن جرير
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Jarir says the pronoun returns to the quality implied by 'loss'; al-Alusi also regards this as remote.
rows.anchor: وعن محمد بن جرير أن الهاء يعود إلى الصفة لدلالة الخسران عليها وهو بعيد أيضا

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Another reading makes ma a relative pronoun for their deeds, with the pronoun referring back to them; its antecedent is explicit in their speech, unlike earlier readings.
rows.anchor: ما موصولة بمعنى التي والمراد بها الأعمال والضمير عائد إليها كأنه قيل يا حسرتنا على الأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Carrying their burdens is a circumstantial clause, either simultaneous with their lament or prospective; burden means sin, as Ibn Abbas reports, and the back is named because it commonly bears loads, intensifying the image of weight and pain.
rows.anchor: والوزر في الأصل الثقل ويقال الذنب وهو المراد هنا أي يحملون ذنوبهم وخطاياهم كما روي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden on the back is a representative metaphor for the severe hardship and punishment their sins bring; another view takes the carrying literally because deeds take bodily form.
rows.anchor: والمراد بيان سوء حالهم وشدة ما يجدونه من المشقة والآلام والعقوبات العظيمة بسبب الذنوب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi describes an evil deed taking the form of an ugly, foul companion in the grave, then mounting its owner at resurrection and driving him to the Fire.
rows.anchor: ليس من رجل ظالم يموت فيدخل قبره إلا جاءه رجل قبيح الوجه أسود اللون منتن الريح عليه ثياب دنسة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن قيس
rows.claim: Amr ibn Qays says a believer is met by his good deed in a beautiful, fragrant form, which reminds him that it carried him in worldly life and now he should ride it.
rows.anchor: إن المؤمن إذا خرج من قبره استقبله عمله في أحسن شيء صورة وأطيبه ريحا

rows.speaker: عمرو بن قيس
rows.claim: In the same report, the unbeliever meets his foul deed, which says that it used to ride him in life and will ride him now.
rows.anchor: كذلك كنت في الدنيا أنا عملك السيء طالما ركبتني في الدنيا فانا اليوم أركبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret all such descriptions figuratively, but the author sees no obstacle to their literal sense and notes that many Sunnis hold that deeds are embodied in the next world, as the apparent weighing language suggests.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم يجعل كل ما ورد في هذا الباب مما ذكر تمثيلا أيضا ولا مانع من الحمل على الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase completes and reinforces the preceding warning; 'sa'a' may be a transitive verb meaning how bad their burden is, with ma as relative, verbal noun, or indefinite subject.
rows.anchor: تذييل مقرر لما قبله وتكملة له و ( ساء ) تحتمل كما قيل هنا ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أن تكون المتعدية المتصرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively sa'a is made intransitive and takes an exclamatory force: how awful is what they carry, or their burden.
rows.anchor: أنها حولت إلى فعل اللازم بضم العين واشربت معنى التعجب والمعنى ما أسوأ الذي يزرونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis treats sa'a as intensified blame, equal in meaning and grammatical behavior to bi's.
rows.anchor: حولت أيضا للمبالغة في الذم فتساوي بئس في المعنى والأحكام

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ glosses Abraham's people's dispute as arguing with him; alternatively they began combating him over monotheism with false traditional arguments and threats.
rows.anchor: أي خاصمون كما قال الربيع أو شرعوا في مغالبته في أمر التوحيد تارة بإيراد أدلة فاسدة واقعة في حضيض التقليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham rebukes them for attempting debate despite their limited standing, the matter's importance, the opponent's strength, and the clarity of truth.
rows.anchor: منكرا عليهم محاجتهم له عليه السلام مع قصورهم عن تلك المرتبة وعزة المطلب وقوة الخصم ووضوح الحق

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nafiʿ and Ibn Amir, in one transmission, read the doubled nūn lightly, deleting one of the two nūns in 'do you dispute with me?'.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر في رواية ابن ذ : وان بتخفيف النون ففيه حذف أحدى النونين

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says the deleted nūn is the indicative ending; the retained nūn is needed in a kasra form before yā, deletion is attested elsewhere, and the pronoun nūn is not protective.
rows.anchor: فقيل : نون الرفع وهو مذهب شيبويه ورجح بأن الحاجة دعت إلى نون مكسورة من أجل الياء

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash identifies the deleted nūn as the protective nūn, preferring deletion of the redundant source of phonetic weight.
rows.anchor: وقيل نون الوقاية وهو مذهب الأخفش ورجح بأنها الزائدة التي حصل بها الثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'He guided me' is a circumstantial clause strengthening Abraham's refusal to debate: divine guidance and support should make them cease arguing and make him disregard their challenge.
rows.anchor: كونه عليه الصلاة والسلام مهديا من جهة الله تعالى ومؤيدا من عنده سبحانه

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Some take the guidance to mean God showed Abraham how to establish the proof of divine unity against them.
rows.anchor: والمراد وقد هدان إلى إقامة الدليل عليكم بوحدانيته عز شأنه

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Another explanation says Abraham had hypothetically followed their path, then saw its total invalidity; neither reading implies that he was previously astray or ignorant of God.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هدان إلى الحق بعد ما سلكت طريقكم بالفرض والتقدير وتبين بطلانها تبينا تاما

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abraham's statement that he does not fear their gods answers his people's threat of harm from their idols, comparable to the threat made to Hud.
rows.anchor: جواب كما روي عن ابن جريج عما خوفوه عليه السلام من إصابة مكروه من جهة معبودهم الباطل

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: The threat may have been for abandoning their worship, for mocking and belittling the idols, or after Abraham damaged them; a report describes him mocking idols made by Azar by throwing them into a river and telling them to drink.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أنه عليه السلام لما شب وكبر جعل آزر يصنع الأصنام فيعطيها له ليبيعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object in 'what you associate' may be relative, with its deleted antecedent referring to what they associate with God; it may also be an indefinite modifier or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وما موصولة اسمية حذف عائدها والضمير المجرور لله تعالى أي لا أخاف الذي تشركونه به سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be connected: Abraham fears harm from their idols only at a time when God wills it, so the idols have no independent agency; it may instead be an unconnected exception meaning he fears his Lord's willing that he fear them.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء متصل في رأي وشيأ مفعول به أو مفعول مطلق أي لا أخاف ما تشركون به في وقت من الاوقات

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري وابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari allows temporal use of an explicit verbal noun but not an implicit one; Ibn Jinni does not distinguish them and permits both.
rows.anchor: ومنع ذلك ابن الانباري مفرقا بين المصدر الصريح فيجوز نصبه على الظرفية وغير الصريح فلا يجوز فيه ذلك وابن جني لا يفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God 'my Lord' signals that any willed harm would carry a nurturing purpose, or Abraham's submission to God's rule and ownership.
rows.anchor: وفي التعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة إلى ضميره عليه السلام إشارة إلى أن مشيئته تلك إن وقعت غير خالية عن مصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's all-encompassing knowledge explains the exception: He may know a reason to send harm through the idols; 'knowledge' is either specification converted from the subject or a cognate-like verbal noun.
rows.anchor: كأنه تعليل للاستثناء أي أحاط بكل شيء علما فلا يبعد أن يكون في علمه سبحانه انزال المكروه بي من جهتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming 'my Lord' instead of using a pronoun reinforces the point and gives pleasure in mentioning God.
rows.anchor: وفي الإظهار في موضع الإضمار تأكيد للمعنى المذكور واستلذاذ بذكره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether they will not remember that their idols cannot cause harm or benefit; 'remember' suggests their inability is already embedded in reason and only needs prompting.
rows.anchor: وفي إيراد التذكر دون التفكر ونحوه إشارة إلى أن أمر آلهتهم مركوز في العقول لا يتوقف إلا على التذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resumed question denies Abraham's fear according to the idolaters' own assumptions, after denying it in reality; asking how he could fear intensifies the total denial because every existent thing has some modality.
rows.anchor: استئناف كما قال شيخ الإسلام مسوق لنفي الخوف عنه عليه السلام بحسب زعم الكفرة بالطريق الإلزامي بعد نفيه عنه بحسب الواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'How' is circumstantial; the object may be relative, indefinite with a modifier, or a verbal noun, with its antecedent omitted.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام لإنكار الوقوع ونفيه بالكلية وفي توجيه الإنكار إلى كيفية الخوف من المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure to fear their association of created things with God is a circumstantial clause reinforcing Abraham's denial and exposing their admission: if they do not fear in the place of fear, he is still less afraid in safety.
rows.anchor: وهو مقرر لإنكار الخوف ونفيه عنه عليه السلام ومفيد لاعترافهم بذلك فإنهم حيث لم يخافوا في محل الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'an authority He did not send down' is a sarcastic name for their nonexistent proof and signals that religious claims must rest on proof revealed by God.
rows.anchor: أي حجة على طريق التهكم قيل مع الإيذان بأن الأمور الدينية لا يعول فيها إلا على الحجة المنزلة من عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name 'God' appears in the second clause to magnify the offense of associating with Him; a proposed grammatical explanation that it supplies an antecedent for the next pronoun is rejected.
rows.anchor: لأن المراد في الجملة الحالية تهويل الأمر وذكر المشرك به أدخل في ذلك

rows.speaker: some precise scholars
rows.claim: One explanation for omitting God's name from the first clause is that the preceding verse already mentioned it, and Abraham avoids even suggesting association with God; its explicit mention in the second fits the idolaters' failure to sanctify Him.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : الظأهر أن يقال في وجه الذكر في الثانية والترك في الاولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects explaining the second mention merely as a needed pronoun antecedent or as a different scope of denial, since the antecedent was already available and the two clauses do not combine under one negation as claimed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن ذكر الاسم الجليل في الجملة الثانية ليعود إليه الضمير في مالم ينرل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explicitly says no divine warrant was revealed for shirk; the author chooses the position that such warrant is rationally impossible, while the Imam's analogy of idols as a prayer direction lies outside the dispute.
rows.anchor: والذي اختاره الأول وقول الامام إنه لا يمتنع عقلا أن يؤمر باتخاذ تلك التماثيل والصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question which group deserves security follows from the contrast between fear in a safe place and lack of fear in a dangerous one, compelling admission that Abraham merits safety and they do not.
rows.anchor: مسوق لالجائهم إلى الاعتراف باستحقاقه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative 'more entitled' gently assumes some possible entitlement to draw them from obstinacy; 'the two groups' avoids naming and blaming them directly and shows security belongs to every monotheist.
rows.anchor: لاستنزالهم عن رتبة المكابرة والاعتساف بسوق الكلام على سنن الانصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question ends by asking which group is more deserving, or what they know; it may challenge them to answer if they are knowledgeable.
rows.anchor: أي من هو أحق بذلك أو شيء من الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading pronounces the lām in 'sulṭān' with ḍamma, a dialectal vowel harmonization following the preceding ḍamma.
rows.anchor: بضم اللام وهي لغة اتبع فيها الضم الضم

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق وابن زيد والجبائي
rows.claim: The explanation that true believers are secure may be God's own resumption, clarifying the correct answer to Abraham's question.
rows.anchor: من جهته تعالى مبين للجواب الحق الذي لا محيد عنه وروي ذلك عن محمد بن إسحاق وابن زيد والجبائي

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali says the clarification is spoken by Abraham.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون من جهة إبراهيم عليه السلام وروي ذلك عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammatical objection says this is not a resumption because it answers an actual question, whereas grammatical resumption should begin speech disconnected from what precedes; the author answers that disconnection means no syntactic attachment, not no semantic link.
rows.anchor: إن الاستئناف النحوي ما كان في ابتداء الكلام ومنقطعا عما قبله وهذا مرتبط بما قبله لارتباط الجواب والسؤال ضرورة

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham defines grammatical resumption as a new opening not connected to what precedes; the author replies that this means syntactic independence, although semantic connection remains.
rows.anchor: لما قال ابن هشام إن الاستئناف النحوي ما كان في ابتداء الكلام ومنقطعا عما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The referent may identify which group deserves security: those who believe in what must be believed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بابتداء الكلام ابتداؤه تحقيقا أو تقديرا أي الفريق الذين آنوا بما يجب الايمان به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن المسيب وقتادة ومجاهد وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators, including Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Musayyib, Qatada and Mujahid, interpret 'wrongdoing' as shirk; idolaters claimed worshipping others alongside God completed their faith by bringing them nearer and interceding.
rows.anchor: وإلى تفسير الظلم بالشرك هنا ذهب ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وابن المسيب وقتادة ومجاهد وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Companions were troubled by this verse and asked who had never wronged himself; the Prophet clarified that the intended grave wrongdoing was shirk, as Luqman told his son.
rows.anchor: أخرجه الشيخان وأحمد والترمذي عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه أن اة ية لما نرلت شق ذلك على الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the hadith does not prove that other wrongdoing is not injustice, the indefinite noun is magnifying: 'great injustice' points to shirk, or the unqualified term denotes its fullest instance.
rows.anchor: لأنهم قالوا : إن التنوين في ( بظلم ) للتعظيم فكأنه قيل : لم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم عظيم

rows.speaker: الجبائي والبلخي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i and al-Balkhi, followed by al-Zamakhshari and most Mu'tazilites, interpret wrongdoing as sin rather than shirk.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد به المعصية وحكي ذلك عن الجبائي والبلخي وارتضاه الزمخشري تبعا لجمهور المعتزلة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue that security is exclusive to those without sin, so a grave sinner cannot be secure or escape punishment; they say 'mixing' is compatible with sins but not with shirk.
rows.anchor: واستدلوا بالآية على أن صاحب الكبيرة لا أمن له ولا نجاة من العذاب حيث دلت بتقديم لهم الآتي على اختصاص الأمن

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They reject the hadith as a solitary report that cannot oppose categorical proof and say shirk cannot coexist with faith because the two are opposites.
rows.anchor: والحديث خبر واحد فلا يعمل به في مقابلة الدليل القطعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that a sinner is neither believer nor unbeliever fails because faith is often used for assent itself, while assent may coexist with shirk, as the Qur'an says many believe in God while associating others with Him.
rows.anchor: بل لا يكاد يفهم منه بلفظ الفعل غير هذا حتى أنه يعطف عليه عمل الصالحات كما جاء في غير ما آية وأجيب بأنه أريد بالإيمان تصديق القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If faith means assent to all required beliefs, mixing need not mean simultaneous belief and shirk: unbelief may cover and overwhelm belief, or a person may alternate between faith and unbelief.
rows.anchor: بل تغطيته بالكفر وجعله مغلوبا مضمحلا أو اتصافه بالإيمان ثم الكفر ثم الإيمان ثم الكفر مرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if security is reserved for people without sin, that does not establish that sinners are certainly punished; it only leaves them fearful and exposed to that possibility.
rows.anchor: إنما يدل على اختصاص الأمن بغير العصاة وهو لا يوجب كون العصاة معذبين البتة بل خائفين ذلك موقعين للاحتمال

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Another view takes security to mean safety from eternal punishment, not freedom from any punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد من الأمن الأمن من خلود العذاب لا الأمن من العذاب مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred syntax makes the relative pronoun a subject, then 'those' a second subject whose predicate is 'they have security'; alternatives treat 'those' as apposition or the relative phrase as predicate of an omitted subject, which al-Alusi calls remote.
rows.anchor: والموصول مبتدأ واسم الإشارة مبتدأ ثان والإشارة إلى الموصول من حيث اتصافه بما في حيز الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are guided to truth; everyone else is in manifest error. Some specify the path that guarantees safety from eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: إلى الحق ومن عداهم في ضلال مبين وقدر بعضهم إلى طريق توجب الأمن من خلود العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After exposing their false claims, the Prophet is told to invite them to hear the prohibitions the situation requires; food prohibitions were already explained, and the invitation signals that these must be avoided.
rows.anchor: أمر له صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ما ظهر بطلان ما ادعوا أن يبين لهم من المحرمات ما يقتضي الحال بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿalaw originally tells someone lower to come up from a higher place, then broadened into a general invitation; it may still imply their low station in ignorance and ascent through listening.
rows.anchor: والأصل فيه أن يقول من هو في مكان عال لمن هو أسفل منه ثم اتسع فيه بالتعميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'I will recite' answers the invitation command: if they come, the Prophet will recite to them.
rows.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : ( أتل ( جواب الأمر أي ان تأتوني أتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God prohibited may be a relative clause with an omitted antecedent, meaning the verses that contain the prohibition, or an interrogative object of 'prohibited' within the recitation clause.
rows.anchor: وما في قوله تعالى : ( ما حرم ربكم ( إما موصولة والعائد محذوف أي أقرأ الذي حرمه ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative analysis means: come so I may tell you and explain what God has prohibited; the clause can serve as an object of recitation because recitation is a kind of saying.
rows.anchor: والمعنى هنا على الاستفهام تعالوا أقل لكم وأبين جواب أي شيء حرم ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Upon you' most suitably modifies 'prohibited,' rather than 'recite,' because it emphasizes avoidance and fits the appeal to God's lordship over the listeners.
rows.anchor: ورجح الأول بأنه أنسب بمقام الاعتناء بإيجاب الانتهاء عن المحرمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is named first because it is the greatest prohibition and the gravest major sin; 'anything' may mean any form of association or any thing whatsoever.
rows.anchor: وبدأ سبحانه بأمر الشرك لأنه أعظم المحرمات وأكبر الكبائر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains kindness to parents as dutifulness with gentleness: no harsh answer, hard stare, or raised voice, but humility before them like a slave before a master.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس يريد البر بهما مع اللطف ولين الجانب فلا يغلظ لهما في الجواب ولا يحد النظر إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to honor parents follows the prohibition of shirk because God's blessing is greatest and parental blessing next: God is the true cause of existence, while parents are its apparent cause.
rows.anchor: لأن نعمة الوالدين أعظم النعم على العبد بعد نعمة الله تعالى لأن المؤثر الحقيقي في وجود الإنسان هو الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on killing children concerns burying them alive from poverty or fear of poverty; some say the two verses address different groups, distinguishing current poverty from future fear, and their provision is named first accordingly.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب في كل آية لصنف وليس خطابا واحدا فالمخاطب بقوله سبحانه : ( من املاق ) من ابتلي بالفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance that God provides both groups explains the prohibition, removes the claimed motive, and guarantees their livelihood.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان فجملة ( نحن ) الخ استئناف مسوق لتعليل النهي وإبطال سببية ما اتخذوه سببا لمباشرة المنهي عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi say 'indecencies' means adultery, whether openly practiced in taverns by low-status people or secretly with lovers by elites.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس والضحاك والسدي وقيل : المراد بها المعاصي كلها

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Razi and others interpret the indecencies as all sins and discuss several prior interpretations of outward and inward sin.
rows.anchor: وفي المراد بما ظهر منها وما بطن على هذا أقوال تقدمت الإشارة إليها واختار ذلك الإمام وجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers adultery as the referent because it fits the sequence of neighboring prohibitions; as a grave crime, it also resembles killing offspring, since illicit children are effectively lost.
rows.anchor: ورجح بعض المحققين الأول بأنه الأوفق بنظم المتعاطفات

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report calls withdrawal before conception a hidden form of burying a child alive, supporting the placement of adultery between the two killing prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قال في حق العزل : ذاك وأد خفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The all-sins reading does not explain why this general prohibition is placed between two specific bans, whereas the adultery reading does; 'do not approach' intensifies deterrence or warns that approach invites commission.
rows.anchor: وعلى القول الآخر لا يظهر وجه توسيط هذا العام بين أفراده ويكون توسيطه بين النهيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protected life is one safeguarded by Islam or covenant: this excludes a hostile combatant and includes a protected non-Muslim; Ibn Jubayr's restriction to believers is misplaced.
rows.anchor: أي حرم قتلها بأن عصمها بالإسلام أو بالعهد فيخرج الحربي ويدخل الذمي فما روي عن ابن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Except by right' may qualify all circumstances, causes, or kinds of killing; the reported lawful grounds are apostasy after faith, adultery after marriage, and killing a protected person.
rows.anchor: وذلك كما روي في الخبر بالكفر بعد الإيمان والزنا بعد الإحصان وقتل النفس المعصومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'That' refers to the five weighty commands; the emphatic nominal sentence renews the covenant, while al-Razi says it makes acceptance easier by conveying gentleness and mercy.
rows.anchor: أي ما ذكر من التكاليف الخمسة الجليلة الشأن من بين التكاليف الشرعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'So that you reason' means using reason to restrain the self from committing forbidden, shameful acts.
rows.anchor: أي تستعملون عقولكم التي تعقل نفوسكم وتحبسها عن مباشرة القبائح المحرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not approach an orphan's wealth in any way except by the best practice for his benefit, such as protecting and investing it; the alternative that the guardian must personally embody the best quality is called remote.
rows.anchor: إلا بالتي هي أحسن ( أي بالفعلة التي هي أحسن ما يفعل بماله كحفظه وتثميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience is guardians and trustees; 'until he reaches maturity' ends the implied duty to preserve the property, after which it must be handed to the orphan as in 4:6.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للأولياء والأوصياء لقوله تعالى : ( حتى يبلغ أشده ( فإنه غاية لما يفهم من الاستثناء لا للنهي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says ashudd is a plural with no singular; some Basrans treat it as singular, while other grammarians derive it from forms meaning severity or strength.
rows.anchor: والأشد على ما قاله الفراء جمع لا واحد له وقال بعض البصريين : هو مفرد كأنك

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Antara's verse uses 'shadd al-nahar' for the height of the day, one proposed derivation of ashudd.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول عنترة : عهدي به شد النهار كأنما خضب ورأسه بالعظلم

rows.speaker: الشعبي وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi and a group define reaching ashudd as puberty; another opinion sets it at eighteen, while al-Suddi says thirty.
rows.anchor: والمراد ببلوغ الأشد عند الشعبي وجماعة بلوغ الحلم وقيل : أن يبلغ ثماني عشرة سنة وقال السدي : أن يبلغ ثلاثين

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Some say the maturity ruling is abrogated by the instruction to test orphans until they reach marriage and then give them their assets.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الآية منسوخة بقوله تعالى : ( حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source refers readers to its earlier detailed treatment of the disputed age for handing over an orphan's property.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم الخلاف في زمن دفع مال اليتيم إليه وأشبعنا الكلام في تحقيق الحق في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfill the measured amount and the weight; kayl may mean the measured commodity, and an omitted noun may be supplied with each verbal noun.
rows.anchor: أي أتموا ( الكيل ( أي المكيل فهو مصدر بمعنى اسم المفعول والميزان ( كذلك كما قال أبو البقاء

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows 'with fairness' to describe the subject as dealing justly or the object as complete measure.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : يجوز أن يكون حالا من المفعول أي تاما

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains that sellers must give the entitled party the full due without shortchanging, while buyers must take their due without demanding an excess.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى المعطي بإيفاء ذي الحق حقه من غير نقصان وأمر صاحب الحق بأخذ حقه من غير طلب الزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not burden anyone beyond capacity; following exact measure can be difficult when frequently required, so the command is limited to what is feasible and excess is excused.
rows.anchor: للترخيص فيما خرج عن الطاقة لما أن في مراعاة ذلك كما هو حرجا مع كثرة وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding obligations are feasible rather than burdensome; God does not impose the impossible.
rows.anchor: من التكليفات ليقبلوا عليها كأنه قيل : جميع ما كلفناكم به ممكن غير شاق ونحن لا نكلف ما لا يطاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When speaking in judgment or testimony, people must be just and truthful even when a relative is involved.
rows.anchor: فاعدلوا ( فيه وقولوا الحق ( ولو كان ( المقول له أو عليه ( ذا قربى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfill whatever covenant was made, especially those listed here and promises to God such as oaths and vows; the fronted phrase emphasizes the covenant with God.
rows.anchor: أي ما عهد اليكم من الامور المعدودة أو أي عهد كان فيدخل فيه ما ذكر دخولا أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing sentence says God emphatically enjoined these duties so people will remember them.
rows.anchor: ذلكم ( أي ما فصل من التكاليف الجليلة ( وصاكم به ( أمركم به أمرا مؤكذا ( لعلكم تذكرون

rows.speaker: حمرة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Hafs from Asim read tadhakkarun with a light dhāl; the other readers geminate it throughout the Qur'an, with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمرة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم تذكرون بتخفيف الذال والباقون بالتشديد في كل القرآن

rows.speaker: القطب الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Qutb al-Razi says the first verse ends with 'reason' because people committed its sins heedlessly, while the second ends with 'remember' because they already practiced and took pride in its duties but might forget them.
rows.anchor: لأن القوم كانوا مستمرين على الشرك وقتل الأولاد وقربان الزنا وقتل النفس المحرمة بغير حق غير مستنكفين ولا عاقلين قبحها

rows.speaker: القطب الرازي
rows.claim: Asked why honoring parents, already practiced, is in the first set, al-Razi answers that parents' blessing follows God's and their care in childhood makes ingratitude especially serious.
rows.anchor: أعظم النعم على الإنسان نعمة الله تعالى ويتلوها نعمة الوالدين لأنهما المؤثران في الظاهر

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Razi instead says the first five duties are obvious and call for rational recognition, while the four later duties are subtle and require thought to find the balanced course.
rows.anchor: التكاليف الخمسة المذكورة في الآية الأولى ظاهرة جلية فوجب تعقلها وتفهمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi suggests that the first set is mostly prohibitions, whose restraint suits the idea of reason holding one back, whereas the later commands need emphasis so they persist in memory.
rows.anchor: إن أكثر التكليفات الأول أدى بصيغة النهي وهو في معنى المنع والمرء حريص على ما منع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says 'this is My path' refers to the Prophet's law, fitting the following prohibition; other views refer to the commands and prohibitions in the two preceding verses or the surah's overall themes.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى شرعه عليه الصلاة والسلام على ما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid? No: the passage attributes this view to Muqatil, who takes the path as the commands and prohibitions in the two preceding verses.
rows.anchor: وعن مقاتل أنه إشارة إلى ما في الآيتين من الأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes the path as the whole surah, most of which establishes monotheism and prophecy and explains the law.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إلى ما ذكر في السورة فإن أكثرها في إثبات التوحيد والنبوة وبيان الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle in 'that you do not associate' is read with kasra by Hamza and al-Kisa'i, open and light by Ibn Amir and Yaqub, and open and doubled by the remaining readers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ( إن ) بالكسر وابن عامر ويعقوب بالفتح والتخفيف والباقون به مشدد

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads 'My path' with an open yāʾ; variants also read 'the path of your Lord' or 'the path of your Lord' in the singular address.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ( صراطي ) بفتح الياء وقريء ( وهذا صراط ربكم وهذا صراط ربك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path is attributed to God by its institution and to the Prophet by his practice and invitation; it is straight, without crookedness, and must be followed in practice.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الصراط إلى الرب سبحانه من حيث الوضع وإليه عليه الصلاة والسلام من حيث السلوك والدعوة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the prohibited 'paths' as misguidances; another report from him says they are divergent religions such as Judaism and Christianity.
rows.anchor: أي الضلالات كما أخرجه ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس وفي رواية عنه أنها الأديان المختلفة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the paths as innovations and doubts.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وعبد بن حميد وغيرهما عن مجاهد أنها البدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result clause after the prohibition deletes one of the two original taʾs; the causative bāʾ means the paths divide and scatter you, more forcefully than saying you yourselves divide.
rows.anchor: نصب في جواب النهي والأصل تتفرق فحذفت إحدى التائين والباء للتعدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's path is Islam, straight and unburdened; alternatively it is following revelation and proof. The Prophet's path is identical to God's, and attributing it to him first encourages following.
rows.anchor: أي سبيل الله تعالى الذي لا اعوجاج فيه ولا حرج لما هو دين الاسلام وقيل : هو اتباع الوحي

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet drew one straight line as God's path, then side lines each bearing a devil who calls people to it, and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : خط رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطا بيده ثم قال : هذا سبيل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing reference reiterates the prohibition on following divergent paths and God's command to follow the straight path.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى إتباع السبل وصاكم به لعلكم تتقون

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan explains the closing aim as fearing God's punishment through performing commands and continuing to avoid prohibitions; following the encompassing straight path brings eternal salvation and lasting happiness.
rows.anchor: عقاب الله تعالى بالمثابرة على فعل ما أمر به والاستمرار على الكف عما نهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the straight path gathers all duties, the repeated testament gives emphatic force to the command and closes with piety as protection from the Fire.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الصراط المستقيم هو الجامع للتكاليف وأمر سبحانه باتباعه ونهى عن اتباع غيره من الطرق ختم ذلك بالتقوى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A hasan report from Ibn Masud says whoever wishes to see the Prophet's testament bearing his seal should recite the verses beginning 'Say: come, I will recite' through 'that you may be mindful.'
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : من سره أن ينظر إلى وصية محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام بخاتمه

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: Ubadah reports that the Prophet sought a pledge on these three verses: fulfillment earns God's reward; a shortcoming punished in this life is expiated, while a deferred matter is left to God's choice to punish or pardon.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيكم يبايعني على هؤلاء الآيات الثلاث ثم تلاهن إلى آخرهن

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb swears that the opening verse of these prohibitions is the first verse of the Torah, beginning with the basmala and the command to recite what God has forbidden.
rows.anchor: سمع كعب رجلا يقرأ ( قل تعالوا أتل ) الخ فقال : والذي نفس كعب بيده إنها لأول آية في التوراة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says these decisive verses have never been abrogated in any scripture, are forbidden to all humanity, are the Mother of the Book, and lead their practitioners to Paradise and abandoners to the Fire.
rows.anchor: هذه آيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب وهن محرمات على بني آدم كلهم وهن أم الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction 'that you do not associate' may use a particle of explanation or a nominalizing particle; each choice raises syntactic and semantic objections.
rows.anchor: هذا و ( أن ) في قوله سبحانه ( أن لا تشركوا ) يحتمل أن تكون مفسرة وأن تكون مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If nominalizing, the phrase seems to name the forbidden act as association rather than refraining from it, and affirmative commands then follow a negative prohibition; treating 'do not' as a relative clause was a view attributed to Sibawayh but is rejected here.
rows.anchor: وظاهر أن المحرم هو الاشراك لا نفيه وأن الأوامر بعد معطوفة على ( لا تشركوا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If explanatory, the following 'this is My path' does not syntactically explain the preceding negative command, and the affirmative commands do not explain a recitation of prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وإن جعلت ( أن ) مفسرة و ( لا ) ناهية النواهي بيان لتلاوة المحرمات توجه إشكالان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari chooses the explanatory particle and includes later commands by understanding their opposites as implicit prohibitions; he connects 'this is My path' to 'follow it' with an omitted causal lām.
rows.anchor: واختار الزمخشري كونها مفسرة وعطف الأوامر لأنها معنى نواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's solution makes the path clause a reason to follow the path, with the pronoun referring back to the previously mentioned straight path.
rows.anchor: بأن قوله سبحانه ( وأن هذا صراطي ) ليس عطفا على ( أن لا تشركوا ) بل هو تعليل للاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says al-Zamakhshari's analysis conjoins the command to follow with the prohibition not to associate, yielding both wāw and fa; the reply is that wāw plus fa is common when an object intervenes.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون اتبعوه عطفا على ( لاتشركوا ) ويكون التقدير فاتبعوا صراطي لأنه مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include 'your Lord magnify' and 'the mosques belong to God, so do not call anyone'; if the doubled conjunction is rejected, the fronted object may attach to an omitted verb such as 'hold fast,' followed by 'follow it.'
rows.anchor: مثل ( وربك فكبر وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا ) فان أبيت الجمع البتة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari answers the second objection by treating affirmative commands as carrying an implicit prohibition of their opposites, such as not mistreating parents, shortchanging measures, abandoning justice, or breaking covenants.
rows.anchor: دل على أن التحريم راجع إلى أضدادها بمعنى أن الأوامر كأنها ذكرت وقصد لوازمها التي هي النهي عن الأضداد

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the commands may instead coordinate with 'I recite what God prohibited,' not with the prohibitions themselves, so the first clause introduces prohibitions and a second introduces commands.
rows.anchor: والثاني ان تكون الأوامر معطوفة على المناهي داخلة تحت حكم التفسيرية ويصح هذا على تقدير محذوف

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Alternatively, the explanatory particle may govern an omitted 'and what He commanded,' understood from the prohibition phrase; then positive and negative commands can both be explained and coordinated.
rows.anchor: ان تكون الأوامر معطوفة على المناهي داخلة تحت حكم التفسيرية ويصح هذا على تقدير محذوف تكون أن مفسرة له

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line 'Do not perish in grief, and be composed' exemplifies coordinating an imperative with a prohibition; the source says this is not disputed, unlike coordination of declarative, interrogative, and imperative clauses.
rows.anchor: يجوز عطف الأمر على النهي والنهي على الأمر لقول أمريء القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says coordinating the path clause with 'come' is extremely unlikely; Abu Hayyan's account using an omitted phrase and interpreting the stated and omitted material together has merit.
rows.anchor: العطف على ( تعالوا ) في غاية البعد ولا ينبغي الالتفات إليه

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi allows an omitted lām before 'that you do not associate': God explains the forbidden because people who prohibit what He made lawful treat obedience to others as equal to obedience to God and become polytheists.
rows.anchor: ونقل الطبرسي جواز كون ( أن لا تشركوا ) بتقدير اللام على معنى أبين لكم الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the Qur'an should not be construed by this strained grammatical analysis.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي تخريج كلام الله تعالى على مثل ذلك كما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting hands and feet 'from opposite sides' means taking a hand from one side and a foot from the other; min is circumstantial, while explaining it causally as punishment for opposition is remote.
rows.anchor: كاليد من جانب والرجل من آخر والجار في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens crucifixion of all as public disgrace and deterrence; salb originally means binding to wood and came to mean hanging someone by the neck until death.
rows.anchor: تفضيحا لكم وتنكيلا لأمثالكم والتصليب مأخوذ من الصلب وهو الشد على خشبة أو غيرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: An Ibn Abbas report says Pharaoh's crucifixion was binding a person under the arms and hanging him until death, a punishment he first introduced, as he did amputation.
rows.anchor: أن الصلب الذي عناه الجبار هو شد الشخص من تحت الإبطين وتعليقه حتى يهلك وهو كقطع الأيدي والأرجل أول من سنه فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed crucifixion for highway robbers because their crime is grave, hence describing it as war against God and His messenger.
rows.anchor: وشرعه الله تعالى لقطاع الطريق تعظيما لجرمهم ولهذا سماه سبحانه محاربة لله ولرسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanqimu means to dislike or reproach; its past forms are given on the patterns of daraba and ʿalima.
rows.anchor: وجاء في الماضي نقم ونقم على وزن ضرب وعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'From us' means the company that believed; the exception is an absolute exception, with its verbal noun as object, explaining that their only supposed fault is believing God's signs.
rows.anchor: منا ( معشر من آمن : ( إلا أن آمنا بأيات ربنا لما جاءتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic construction likewise says there is no flaw except that guests are distracted by longing for loved ones and homeland; it illustrates the exception's syntax.
rows.anchor: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن ضيوفهم تعاب بنسيان الأحبة والوطن

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A report from Ata takes tanqimu as 'punish'; then believing is the cause of their punishment, and on either reading the believers cut off Pharaoh's hope that his threat will succeed.
rows.anchor: يشير ماروى عن عطاء وعليه فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer for God to pour patience over them compares patience to poured water; alternatively they ask for what purifies their sins by helping them endure Pharaoh's threat.
rows.anchor: أي أفض علينا صبرا يغمرنا كما يفرغ الماء أو صب علينا ما يطهرنا من الآثام وهو الصبر على وعيد فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, 'pour' is an explicit derivative metaphor and 'patience' its contextual indicator; on the second, patience is an original concealed metaphor and 'pour' its imaginative elaboration.
rows.anchor: على الأول استعارة تبعية تصريحية و ( صبرا ) قرينتها والمراد هب لنا صبرا تاما كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggestion that both readings work alike through the idea of flooding or purification is judged unconvincing, despite the stature of its proponent.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الكلام على الأول كالكلام على الثاني إلا أن الجامع هناك الغمر وههنا التطهير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kalbi and al-Suddi say 'take us in death as Muslims' asks God to keep them firm in Islam and not let Pharaoh's threat tempt them away; they report that Pharaoh carried out his threat.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس والكلبي والسدي أنه فعل بهم ما أوعدهم به

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Others say Pharaoh could not carry out the threat because God promised Moses, Aaron, and their followers victory; the first group says victory may mean victory in argument or the final outcome, without excluding some deaths.
rows.anchor: لقوله تعالى : ( لايصلون إليكما بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون )
